title: The Causal Clock
subtitle: Five rings, one chain, one heart.
intro_lines: Turn the rings — drag, scroll, or use the arrow keys.
Right-click a ring to pin it still. You have two pins.
Lead the chain from the crown to the heart.
_comment_margin_notes: Placeholder lines handwritten on the parchment notes beside the clock. Replace or leave empty.
margin_notes: Time folds not in a line, but in a circle.
_comment_rings: Outermost first. 'start' is the scrambled starting position. Segments use local slots: slot s sits at s * 360/positions degrees in the ring's own frame. out = where the chain meets the ring's outer edge, in = where it leaves through the inner edge. 'decoy': true marks a red herring: it looks and connects like any other chain, but its slot shift (in - out) differs from the genuine one, so with the heart fixed any route through it can only ever arrive at a sealed lock. The validator proves this for every layout.
_comment_hub: The heart is fixed. Its one open lock is 'sockets'; 'sealed' locks are where the red-herring routes end.
_comment_couplings: a turns d steps -> b turns d*ratio. one_way = ratchet (b cannot drive a). cam = only engaged while one of the listed local sectors of the cam ring sits under the gear at angle_deg. Keep gear angles between slot angles (e.g. 22.5, 67.5 ...) so gears never hide a junction.
_comment_milestones: trigger.type: chain_depth (value = rings crossed), segment_linked (ring + segment index), complete. presentation: toast | card | silent. memory_id refers to data/memories/*.json.
_comment_solution: A known (optimal, 13 moves) solution from the start state. Verified by tests/run_tests.gd.
